newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ electricity reform not working - consumer group.
newsitem.headline: NZ electricity reform not working - consumer group.

text.p: The Consumer Coalition on Energy said a signalled electricity price increase by TransAlta NZ, to be formed from the merger of EnergyDirect and Capital Power, called into question the effectiveness of the planned new wholesale market.
TransAlta said on Thursday it expected Wellington consumers to face a 3.3 percent price increase from April.
Consumers Institute David Russell renewed the Coalition's call for an independent monitor for the electricity sector.

"The avalanche of mergers and acquisitions and resultant staff layoffs, plus the new technology, should be delivering efficiencies and lower costs. But customers are not sharing in any tangible benefits," Russell said in a statement.
He said Electricity Supply Association figures showed prices throughout New Zealand had risen on average by 3.7 percent above the rate of inflation for the past five years.
The role of an independent monitor would be to "provide a major safeguard against the mercenary aims of what is still a series of monopoly businesses with captive customers".
